page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 15 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, it allocates one physical core with two threads. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench (2229.0) and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.51 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.46 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak or poor, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1960.58 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 18.79 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.5 GB per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight databases, text processing, and small-scale language model inference where single-core execution speed is prioritized over multi-threaded throughput.
